record.one_liner: Discord apps let you customize and extend Discord using a collection of APIs and interactive features.

auth_methods.quote: Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of three ways: Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app’s settings. For more information on bots see bots vs user accounts . Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the OAuth2 API . Using basic authentication with credentials as the client ID and client secret found on the OAuth2 page of your app’s settings in the format client_id:client_secret as a Base64 encoded string.

access_test.quote: First, you’ll need to create an app in the developer portal if you don’t have one already: Enter a name for your app, then press Create .

access_ship.quote: Once you add scopes, copy the URL from the Install Link section from before. Since our app is supporting both installation contexts, we’ll install your new app to both a test server and your user account so that we can test in both installation contexts . Install to server To install your app to your test server, copy the default Install Link for your app from the Installation page.

api_type.quote: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.

api_breadth.quote: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications. It’s the primary way to interact with Discord from your own code.
